(a) If the final ई or ऊ be not a fem. termination, it remains
unchanged; शम्भु धीः सा शम्भुः;, बहुतन्त्रीषमनी.

1 Tatpurusha.

§ 203. The first variety consists of such Tatpurusha com-
pounds as have the attributive member in any one of the
oblique cases when dissolved. There are six sub-varieties of
this corresponding to the six oblique cases

§ 204. (a) A noun in the Accusative case is compounded
with श्रित, असीत, पतित, गत, अत्यस्त, प्राप्त, आपन्न, गमी, सुभुक्षु, and
others †; as कृष्णं श्रितः कृष्णश्रितः one who has resorted to Kṛishṇa
( as his refuge); दुःखमतीतः दुःखातीतः one who has overcome pain;
सुखं आपन्नः सुखापन्नः one who has obtained happiness, ग्रामं गमी
ग्रामगमी going to a village, a passenger; अन्नं बुभुक्षुः अन्नबुभुक्षुः &c.

N. B. प्राप्त and आपन्न may also be placed first; as प्राप्तो जीविको
प्रासजीविकः or जीविकाप्राप्तः one who has obtained livelihood;
similarly आपन्नजीविकः or जीविकापन्नः; प्राप्तजीविका स्त्री, &c.
